The AMIA Board approved the "Core Content for the Subspecialty of Clinical Informatics" in November 2008, and it was published in JAMIA in March–April 2009 (Gardner et al.).
ABMS approved clinical informatics as a subspecialty open to diplomates of all member boards; the date is given as 2010 in a 2018 Yearbook article and as 21 September 2011 by AMIA.
ABPM and the American Board of Pathology ran the first board exam in October 2013, and 455 physicians received the first certificates in January 2014.

In July 2018, AMIA, ABPM and ABPath ran a formal practice analysis, published by Silverman et al. in 2019, which produced 5 domains, 42 tasks and 139 knowledge and skill statements and added data analytics and governance.
ABPM switched to an updated content outline in 2021.
On the nursing side, ANCC runs an Informatics Nursing board certification: a 2022 role delineation study (Exam 27), and a test content outline effective 3 May 2023, republished on 29 August 2025.
The CMIO is described in a 2010s-era industry piece as "a fairly new addition to the healthcare industry".
CDS and alert governance shows up as committee work led by informaticists, for example Cleveland Clinic's CDS Governance Workgroup led by Associate CMIOs and Vanderbilt's "BPA Clickbusters" (2022).
ANCC's informatics nursing certification start date was not confirmed in these searches.

The regulatory basis for the role appears in this evidence in 2010.
On 3 November 2010 the SEC adopted Rule 15c3-5 (the Market Access Rule), with compliance from 14 July 2011.

It requires broker-dealers with market access to run automated pre-trade financial and regulatory controls under their "direct and exclusive control", to review those controls regularly, and to have the CEO certify them every year.
A firm's 2013-era comment letter to the CFTC called kill switches "an effective last-resort means of risk control", and FIA consolidated its best practices in July 2024.
In Europe and the UK, MiFID II's RTS 6 (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/589) sets staffing and compliance-function requirements.
The FCA's February 2018 multi-firm review found some firms "lacked a robust and comprehensive governance framework".
PRA SS5/18 (effective 30 June 2018) asks firms to assign responsibility for approving algorithms, owning algorithm and risk-control inventories, owning kill switches and reviewing incidents.
As a named job, the role appears in the evidence in bank postings from late 2024 to 2026 (NatWest, Citi, Nomura, BMO).
Titles vary (ETRC, EAT Risk, Algo Risk & Control), and years of experience are typically 6–10 for VP.
Sources: SEC release 34-63241; FIA 2024 paper; RTS 6 text; FCA 2018 review; PRA SS5/18; postings below (all S).

In this evidence, the credential requirement appears as an enforced standard in 2012.

That year a NERC Find, Fix and Track record under PER-003-0 treated transmission switching by non-certified operators, without oversight from a NERC-certified operator, as a violation (White & Case, 2012).
NERC's standards projects on certifying system operators (Project 2007-04) and system personnel training (Project 2006-01, then Project 2010-01) date from 2006–2010.
PER-005-2 (training) was board-adopted on 6 February 2014.
PER-003-2 (credentials) was adopted by the NERC Board on 10 May 2018 and replaced PER-003-1 and PER-004-2.
Its January 2025 exam resource materials say the content outlines come from a NERC-wide job analysis.
Postings from 2024–2026 (MISO, ERCOT, Pedernales Electric, Georgia Power, El Paso Electric, Black Hills Energy) all require the certificate at hire or within about 5–6 months.
The start date of NERC's certification program (often given as the late 1990s) was not confirmed by these searches.

Covers: people registered with FINRA as Securities Traders (Series 57) because they design, develop or significantly modify algorithmic trading strategies, or supervise that work day to day.
Also covers the UK "algorithmic trading" certification function under the FCA's Senior Managers and Certification Regime.

In this evidence, the US registration category first appears in 2015.
FINRA Regulatory Notice 15-06 proposed it, arguing that algorithms which generate orders do work similar to individual traders, so their developers should meet the same knowledge standard.
The SEC approved the change on 7 April 2016.
Regulatory Notice 16-21 (June 2016) made it effective on 30 January 2017.

From then, an associated person primarily responsible for designing, developing or significantly modifying an algorithmic trading strategy in equity, preferred or convertible debt securities, or who supervises or directs that work day to day, must pass the Series 57 and …
In the UK, the FCA's 2016 final rules extended the Certification Regime to an "algorithmic trading" function (now SYSC 27.8.23R, item 8 in the SYSC 27.7.3R table).
In 2023, FIA EPTA asked HM Treasury to consider removing the algorithmic trading function.
In postings it appears as a licence line ("Series 57 (Algo Trader)", "Series 57 license preferred") on senior engineering and quant roles at banks, asset managers and trading firms.
Established as a regulatory category since 2017; thinly visible in job ads.

Seven conditions follow from the record.
Frame continuity. The office pursues the movement's goal, in managerial terms.
Carriers. The movement's people or organizations bring it in.
A forcing lever. A law, liability rule, procurement rule or certification with a vague mandate that firms must interpret.
A carrier profession with an association, a certification and a body of knowledge (ASSE, ASQC, IAPP, TSPA).
A business case. Personnel offices survived by recasting themselves in "purely economic terms" [seen].[^dobbinsutton] The same move empties out the goal (Edelman).
A responsibility structure. Kalev, Dobbin and Kelly found that "efforts to establish responsibility for diversity lead to the broadest increases" [seen]; training and evaluations did least.[^kalev]

Coupling. The structure changes outcomes rather than standing as ceremony (Meyer and Rowan) or being implemented without affecting results (Bromley and Powell).[^meyer][^bromley] Cooptation shares the symbols of power, not the power (Selznick, M).[^selznick]
